chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: Visiting the Mills office and landing the Onyx Club job
summary: Her Pittsburgh radio contact led her to Mills Music, and Joe Helbock hired her at the Onyx Club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Pittsburgh -- Jackie Heller -- who had a radio show. And his sister used to come up to the club -- Shirley Heller -- and she said that she was going to send a letter to Mills, because there was some relationship there. And if I ever go to New York, go to Mills and ask for Mr. Pincus. I still haven't found out who Mr. Pincus was.
This is the publishing house Mills?

That's right. And so I did go to the office, and I asked for Mr. Pincus. They said okay, just wait a minute. So I waited for quite a long time. I had an appointment with Gladys and Claude the same day and I had to leave. And so when I met Gladys and Claude, well the first thing that they did was handed me a contract to sign. By that time, Mr. Pincus had just lost the ball game. But anyway, I evidently beat the letter to

See, I came to New York -- I told you I left Pittsburgh on a Sunday excursion. I met Gladys and Claude on Monday, and I auditioned at the Onyx Club on Wednesday and went to work on Friday.

Right. So anyway, I had already started working at the Onyx Club. And in came Sidney Mills from Mills, say, trying to sell Maxine Williams to Joe Helbock -- and I was on the stand singing at the time.
And Joe Helbock already knew that I had been to the office. So anyway, he let Sidney rave on. He said, "I got a girl coming from Pittsburgh, she's sensational," blah, blah, blah.
And so Joe says, "Well, is she any better than this girl?" He said, "Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah."
So he says, "Well, have a drink on me. She was in your office three days ago." So that got to be a running joke thereon.
